title: ephemeral disk attach debug scratchpad
content:
Notes to self: working through repeated node join failures in the ephemeral worker pool (pool name: ephem-ssd-us-west). Symptoms: nodes come up, kubelet registers briefly, then node flips to NotReady or gets evicted pods due to ImagePullBackOff / volume attach timeouts. This doc collects commands tried, raw error snippets, hypotheses, and next actions.

Timeline / quick summary:
- 2026-02-27: multiple workers in ephem-ssd-us-west cycled due to underlying host maintenance. New instances fail to fully join.
- 2026-03-01: Observed repeated AttachVolume/DetachVolume loops for the ephemeral root-volume (nvme ephemeral).
- 2026-03-07: Tried kubelet config tweak (eviction thresholds) temporarily — reduced chattiness but underlying attach errors persisted.

Commands run (copy-paste friendly):
- Describe node and check conditions:
  kubectl describe node ip-10-0-21-45.us-west.internal
  kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady

- Kubelet journal around bootstrap time:
  sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 400 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'

- Search for attach/detach errors across cluster:
  kubectl -n kube-system get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | grep -i attach
  kubectl get events --all-namespaces | grep AttachVolume

- Inspect cloud provider attach logs (aws/gce/azure depending). For our env (AWS Nitro):
  aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids i-0abc12345 --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].BlockDeviceMappings'
  sudo dmesg | egrep -i 'nvme|attach|disk'

Raw error snippets captured: (copied from kube-controller-manager / node events)
- "AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume \"vol-0f1e2d3c4b5a6\": Timeout waiting for attachment of volume \"vol-0f1e2d3c4b5a6\" to instance i-0abc12345"
- "FailedMount: MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume \"vol-0f1e2d3c4b5a6\" : rpc error: code = Internal desc = device not found"
- kubelet: "Device or resource busy" when trying to format ephemeral (/dev/nvme1n1) during cloud-init reboot path
- Node status: Kubelet ready=true, but KubeProxy/iptables failing with: "failed to ensure iptables rules: could not find device for PodCIDR" (indicative of missing ENI attachment)

What we've tried so far (chronological):
1) Cordon + drain, recreate instance from ASG with same launch template (no luck — new instance hit same attach timeout).
2) Manual attach via AWS console succeeded for one volume but kubelet still logs device not found (timing issue w/ udev?).
3) Added sleep/wait hooks to cloud-init user-data to ensure NVMe discovery runs after NVMe driver loads (patch in launch template test-3).
4) Forced systemd daemon-reload and restart of kubelet after instance boot:
   sudo systemctl restart systemd-udevd && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
   Observed transient better behavior for 1 node, but other nodes still fail.
5) Helmed the node-provisioner chart with debug values (replica=1, hostCleanup=true) to try a controlled repro cluster; saw same attach error.
6) Disabled CSI attach controller temporarily — no change, points more to cloud/disk discovery vs CSI logic.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Race between NVMe device discovery and kubelet mount step. Some kernels/AMI combos delay NVMe device registration, kubelet times out. (evidence: manual attach works, journal shows nvme registration later than kubelet mount attempt).
- H2: Host-level udev rules or kernel driver regression on the new AMI causing name changes (nvme1n1 sometimes shows up as nvme2n1). Kubelet expects device path from cloud provider mapping and fails.
- H3: Underlying ENI/ENI trunking bug causing podCIDR not being set on node -> kube-proxy fails -> node partially ready and evicts pods unrelated to volume attach. (evidence: iptables errors in kube-proxy logs)
- H4: Race in cloud provider attach/detach plugin - detach happening too quickly leaving stale mappings (less likely given timeouts are attach-timeouts).

Troubleshooting artifacts I collected (commands + outputs stored as local snippets):
- /tmp/node-ip-10-0-21-45-kubelet.log (excerpt shows nvme registration after kubelet mount attempt)
- cloud-init output: /var/log/cloud-init-output.log -> shows nvme formatted by user-data scripts on firstboot
- dmesg excerpt: "nvme 0000:00:08.0: Adding to PCIe bus" then "nvme1n1: p1 p2" ~120s after boot

Small experiment ideas to validate H1/H2 quickly:
- Delay kubelet start in AMI/launch template: add systemd drop-in to make kubelet.service 'After=systemd-udevd.service' and add ExecStartPre sleep 60. Reboot and see if attach succeeds consistently.
- Run a loop on a repro node that polls /dev/disk/by-id and maps aws device names to discovered /dev/nvme* names to detect mapping shifts.
- Boot one instance with different kernel (older AMI) to see if regression tied to kernel/driver.

Temporary mitigations in prod (low risk):
- Increase attach timeout in cloud-controller-manager (if supported) and kubelet mount timeout to give devices more time to appear.
- Use instance store-backed AMI with pre-attached ephemeral mapping baked in (tradeoff: not all instance types supported).

Helm/values notes (we attempted a test that replays provisioning via Helm in staging):
- Chart: infra/node-provisioner (values used below)
  replicaCount: 1
  nodeSelector: {pool: ephem-ssd}
  tolerations: [{key: "node.kubernetes.io/unreachable", operator: "Exists", effect: "NoSchedule"}]
  debug: true
- Observed provisioner logs: "waiting for volume attach confirmation" repeated then eventually "timeout". The kube-provisioner attempts -> cloud API -> success -> kubelet still can't find device.

Checklist / next steps (concrete):
- [ ] Reproduce with scheduled boot+systemd delay (drop-in that sleeps 60s before kubelet). Test 5 nodes.
- [ ] Boot one node with older AMI (kernel v5.15 -> v6.1) to see if nvme timings differ.
- [ ] Add udev rule to create stable /dev/by-id symlinks earlier (udev trigger) on AMI and bake.
- [ ] Add extra logging to node-provisioner Helm chart to dump /dev and use /proc/partitions right before kubelet mount attempt.
- [ ] If reliable repro: prepare AMI rollback and coordinate with infra to roll pool.

Random notes / things I don't want to forget:
- There was a past bug (internal ticket OPS-876) where some Nitro instances delayed root NVMe until after cloud-init finished due to a vendor firmware handshake. Might be related.
- Slack thread: #infra -> message ts 1677678234 has a screenshot of attach events (saved in linked_artifacts).
- If debugging locally on repro node, remember to disable kubelet startup race by systemctl mask kubelet then manually run kubelet binary with --v=4 to capture timing.

Quick commands to capture current state on any failing node: (paste these into incident channel)
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 120\- sudo dmesg | tail -n 200\- ls -la /dev/disk/by-id | sed -n '1,200p'\- cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | sed -n '1,400p'\- kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Node,involvedObject.name=<node-name> -n kube-system --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp

Conclusion (working hypothesis): this is likely a device discovery timing/regression on the AMI/kernel interacting with NVMe ephemeral devices. Next best step: reproduce with deliberate kubelet delay to confirm. If confirmed, bake AMI with udev/udev hwdb changes or add kubelet delay as short-term mitigation and notify platform owners for AMI rollback.

Notes saved by: Lena Chen (eng-infrastructure)
